deck.prompt: Found rusted stab-sticks under the old latrine. Give to the boyz, or melt for shiny?

dialogues.text: Buried under the old latrine.
Brown dust on them makes humies sick. Very good.

deck.prompt: Boyz need more meat. Little greens got food. They not need it.

dialogues.text: They eat rats. Or they eat each other. Not Kargoth's problem.
Let them try. Kargoth will squash them like bugs.

deck.prompt: You fight me in the pit! Show who is strongest. Or you scared?

dialogues.text: No eye-squishing. Groin-kicking is very good.
Then you is Boss. But Kargoth never lose.

deck.prompt: Goblin talk too much. Kargoth throw him in fire. You mad?

dialogues.text: He make a very good black rock now.

deck.prompt: Pointy-ear prisoners fly real good. Let Kargoth throw them at humies.

dialogues.text: The pointy ears make them spin! Very fast!

deck.prompt: Drank the blue fire water. Feet melting the rocks. Want to hug a wizard.

dialogues.text: My feet melting the rocks, Boss.

nextCard.prompt: Kargoth squeeze the fire-humie. Big boom! Fire-humie gone. Sorry I break the wall.

deck.prompt: Found furry monster. Ate three goblins already. Kargoth keep it.

dialogues.text: It only eat things that bleed. So, no.

nextCard.prompt: Furry monster break chain. Ate the armor-maker. Monster gone now. We need new armor-maker.

deck.prompt: Red make me go fasta. Buy red paint, or Kargoth use goblin blood.

dialogues.btn: Does it actually make you faster?
dialogues.text: Kargoth science say yes.

deck.prompt: Kargoth invent Orc Yoga. Bones crack loud. Tell all boyz they gotta do it.

dialogues.text: It is when I break humie spine over my knee.

deck.prompt: Kargoth ate the door-key. Very safe now. We wait, or you chop me open?

dialogues.text: It looked like a shiny beetle. Was crunchy.
Kargoth's stomach digest iron. Key might be gone soon.

deck.prompt: We founds a shiny rock! It makes our handsies burn real bad!

dialogues.text: Sickly green! It makes my teeth hum!

deck.prompt: We cooks a new mush-stew! It glows in the dark!

dialogues.text: We used the mushrooms from the spider-holes! They tastes like colors!

deck.prompt: The shiny rocks in the vault... we ate some. Now our tummies is screaming!

dialogues.text: We thought they was very hard cheeses!

deck.prompt: We builds a catapult! It flings the other goblins real high! Can we push the button?!

dialogues.text: Gribble said he wanted to see the big fire in the sky!

nextCard.prompt: Gribble hit the ceiling, bounced off a stalactite, and landed in the gold vault! He crushed your favorite chest!

deck.prompt: We finds a door with a giant head-bone on it! Should Snivel knock?

dialogues.text: Just a sign that says 'Certain Doom.' Probably a humie trick!

deck.prompt: The rat-catchers says they makes a guild! They screaming for more fuzz-mold on the bread!

dialogues.text: Three extra moldy crusts, or they stop eating the plague-rats!

deck.prompt: We gets a glowing ball! It keeps yelling bout a humie in green! Make it stop! Smash it?!

dialogues.text: Something about a 'Link to the Past.' It makes our ears itch!

deck.prompt: Snivel finds a Magic Window! A very handsome goblin looks right back at me!

dialogues.text: I pinched it from the dead elf-man's bag!

nextCard.prompt: I smashed the window. A sharp piece bounced up and cut off the big Orc's ear! He is very mad!

deck.prompt: We finds lots of humie paper with big words! It says Healer's Debt Scroll. Can the Swarm eats it for supper?

dialogues.text: Very dry! But the blood-oath part has a nice crunch!

deck.prompt: We builds a big statue of you! Made of mud and wet bones! It stinks so beautiful!

dialogues.btn: Is that supposed to be my nose?
dialogues.text: Yes! The femur bone really captures your majestic face!

deck.prompt: The boys makes a brotherhood pact! They cries for safety rails so they don't falls in the hot-hot magma!

dialogues.text: Gribble fell in yesterday. He didn't even leave a good splash.

nextCard.prompt: The boys thought the railings was for swinging. Three dozen just swung right into the fire-juice.

deck.prompt: We finds a yellow shiny cup! It makes scooping the poop-pits very fancy!

dialogues.text: It has shiny rocks on the side! Very good for scraping.
We washed it in the slime-river! Good as new!

deck.prompt: A humie drops a Cookbook! Now the cooks is crying and won't feed us the raw meat no more!

nextCard.prompt: The cooks makes a 'roast'. It is still raw. But it is on a plate. With a little flag in it.

dialogues.btn: Won't they miss the raw meat?
dialogues.text: They says it tastes like 'texture and despair.' Very ungrateful.

deck.prompt: We finds a Bar of Soap in a humie kit! Is it an edible holy relic?

dialogues.text: Lavender and shiny judgment!

deck.prompt: The Swarm wants a Spokesman! They say if they dies, they wants their teeths to be shiny first!

dialogues.text: Shiny teeths, so they looks good when they gets trampled in battle.

deck.prompt: The Rat-Stew has started talking back to the cooks! It's demanding a seat on the High Council!

dialogues.text: It says it represents all the stews we has ever wronged. Very dramatic.

deck.prompt: Ew ew! We finds a wildflower in the sludge! It's too bright! It burns our eyeballs! Burn it?!

nextCard.prompt: The flower is in the shadow dungeon now. The goblins is walking past it on tiptoe. Just in case.

dialogues.text: It just sits there being bright. That's enough.

deck.prompt: A dirty Hero is at the big door! He smells like old grog. Should we makes him a scout for the Swarm?

nextCard.prompt: The Hero was full of strong grog! The pit monsters is now drunk and refusing to work. They is singing sea shanties!

dialogues.text: He says he's looking for a dungeon with character. We has plenty of that.

deck.prompt: Ouch-water dripping from the roof! Tastes like spicy fire! Put it in the Rat-Stew for flavor?

nextCard.prompt: The liquid was liquid rage! My Bruisers ate the stew and are in a frenzy, tearing the dungeon apart!

dialogues.text: The crack where Greenfang headbutted the ceiling last Tuesday.

deck.prompt: We steals a magic word-book! The paper is so softs... can the boys use it for the latrines?

nextCard.prompt: The magic papers hated the poop-pits! Half the warrens just blowed up into purple fire!

deck.prompt: A glowing surface-maiden wanders into the traps! She gives us Blessing of Gold if we let her walk away!

nextCard.prompt: Dat blessing was holy light! Vault is full of gold, but da front row of my Vanguard is permanently blind!

deck.prompt: The men of the West are marching on our upper gates.

dialogues.text: Enough to drown our Vanguard in blood. We should use the traps.

deck.prompt: My Uruks demand a larger share of the plunder to stay in line. Pay up.

dialogues.text: Then we take it out of your hide.

deck.prompt: I challenge the Greenfang Bruiser to a duel for supremacy of the Vanguard.

dialogues.text: I will wear his skull as a codpiece.

deck.prompt: We captured a dwarven engineer. I want to torture him. The goblins want him to build traps.

dialogues.text: He muttered something about a 'Meat-Grinder 3000'.

deck.prompt: My troops complain the torture chambers lack ambiance. Permission to impale them at a scenic angle.

dialogues.text: At a 45-degree angle, facing the scenic lava falls.

deck.prompt: The dwarven king sent a scroll demanding we stop chanting at midnight. I intend to eat the messenger.

dialogues.text: It was heavily perfumed and asked politely. Disgusting.

nextCard.prompt: Pathetic. The dwarven messenger was wearing concealed spiked armor. I am now in the infirmary with a perforated colon.

deck.prompt: My Vanguard wants Tuesdays off. To pillage for fun, they say. Not for quota.

dialogues.text: Only if you aren't doing it for a strict quota.

deck.prompt: My scouts captured an elven bard. He won't stop playing the lute. It is demoralizing.

nextCard.prompt: Executed loudly. The lute kept playing on its own for several hours afterward. The men are unsettled.

dialogues.text: A ballad about a brave elf. In our dungeon. About the elf's feelings.

deck.prompt: I demand better siege engines. We cannot conquer the surface with sharpened logs.

nextCard.prompt: The engineers built a trebuchet. It flung a boulder directly into our own gate. They seem proud.

dialogues.text: The last assault we lost fourteen men to splinters. Splinters, Overlord.

deck.prompt: My lieutenant challenged me for command. I can crush him, but he is a skilled fighter.

nextCard.prompt: He is dead. Three others are already eyeing my position. I may have created a tradition.

dialogues.text: He once fought three trolls blindfolded. He lost, but he tried very hard.

deck.prompt: The Swarm's screeching gives my Bruisers migraines. Let me repurpose the Warrens as a quiet zone.

dialogues.text: They sing about fungus. Terribly.

nextCard.prompt: The kicked-out goblins is sleeping in the treasury! We is eating the gold coins, thinking they is hard shiny beetles!

deck.prompt: My Bruisers formed a war-pact. They demand Hazard Pay for fighting mages. Being turned into sheep is unprofessional.

dialogues.text: Enough to start a wool export business.

nextCard.prompt: The new sheep recruits are terrible at fighting, but I have made a fortune selling their wool.

deck.prompt: I found a surface Knight who claims he's neutral. He wants a writ to hunt the slime in the basement for research.

dialogues.text: He wears two swords on his back, which seems excessive and try-hard.

deck.prompt: I want to host a clan reunion. Three days of mandatory screaming and traditional poison-tasting.

dialogues.text: Statistically? Four. But they'll be very close.

deck.prompt: Dwarven sappers have breached the lower armory. They are strapped with explosives. If they blow, we lose the Black Iron.

nextCard.prompt: My Bruisers killed the dwarves, but the explosion turned our best elites into a fine mist. The iron is safe, though.

deck.prompt: Da boyz is hungry! Rat meat is garbage! We wants real meat, with lots of screaming!

dialogues.btn: How bad is the rat meat?
dialogues.text: Gribble says it tastes like regret wrapped in fur.

deck.prompt: Humies put up wood walls outside! Greenfang wants to smash it into toothpicks!

dialogues.text: Lots! They make funny squeaks when Greenfang throw rocks at them.
Not as sturdy as Greenfang's head!

deck.prompt: Iron pinching my gut. Make da smithy give Greenfang pure gold armor! Shiny make boyz fight harder!

dialogues.text: But it's SHINY! Imagine the glare in their eyes!

deck.prompt: Da boyz got no one to hit! Can we makes a fight pit? Winner drinks da loser's grog!

dialogues.text: Da Swarm usually eats em before they get cold.

deck.prompt: Da boyz makes a Choir! We stands in a circle and screams at a big rock. Give us gold for our art!

dialogues.text: 'Blood on the Rocks' in G-flat. Very emotional.

deck.prompt: Greenfang punch a wall! Found secret room with humie number-books. Make my head hurt. Burn em?

dialogues.text: Yeah, looking at the tax rates makes my eyes bleed.

deck.prompt: Boyz caught a big troll! It say it wants to be an accountant. Dat sound like nerd talk. Smash?

dialogues.text: It counted to three before biting off its own finger.

nextCard.prompt: Da troll ate the paper books and yelled BANKRUPT! Humie tax men got scared and ran away!

deck.prompt: Greenfang headbutt a rock-spike. The rock won. Da boyz is laughing!

dialogues.text: It had a very solid defensive stance.

deck.prompt: We loot a humie wagon. Gots lots of fancy silk hats! Da boyz wanna wear em when we chop heads!

nextCard.prompt: Da boyz fought twice as hard! Also three of them was blinded by the reflective trim. Still a win.

dialogues.text: Greenfang's hat is stuck on his horns. He looks magnificent.

deck.prompt: Greenfang gonna grease da front door ramp with leftover Rat-Stew! Humies gonna slip and go SPLAT!

dialogues.text: Gribble tested it. He went very fast and did not stop.

deck.prompt: Goblins talking about a Brotherhood Pact! Greenfang don't know what dat is, but I wanna smash it!

nextCard.prompt: Da Brotherhood Pact already has a flag. And a song. The song is just screaming but it has a structure.

dialogues.text: A goblin what visited the surface and came back with ideas. Very dangerous.

deck.prompt: Caught a music humie! Say he sing about you being super mean if we don't eat his legs. We eat em anyway?

nextCard.prompt: Da music man's legs was chewy, but his screaming sounded real nice during da feast!

dialogues.text: A brave hero who smells like flowers and defeats the darkness with feelings.

deck.prompt: Da boyz wants fancy Battle Shrouds! We ain't choppin no one unless we look pretty and dead!

nextCard.prompt: Da boyz looks terrifying! Also three of them tripped on the hem and fell down the stairs. Very stylish.

dialogues.text: Blood red, they says. Very on-brand.

deck.prompt: Caught a surface thief sneaking into the lower vaults. Flay him?

dialogues.btn: What did he try to steal?
dialogues.text: A single copper coin. The audacity is what exhausts me.

deck.prompt: I remember the layout of the Sun-King's armory. Give me 100 men and I'll bring back steel.

dialogues.text: Soft as butter. But they have shiny spears.

nextCard.prompt: The raid was a success. The Sun-King's guards fought fiercely, but I brought back carts of steel. I am only missing half my jaw.

deck.prompt: Old wounds ache. Winter is cold. I need the Shadow Priest's dark magic to fight.

nextCard.prompt: The priest healed me. I feel twenty years younger and deeply suspicious. Something was taken in exchange.

dialogues.text: Three nightmares and a tooth. Standard rates.

deck.prompt: Found some surface grog. Makes the boyz fight harder. Die faster too.

nextCard.prompt: The grog worked. The boyz fought like demons. Then they kept fighting. Each other. For six hours.

dialogues.text: Three men went blind from the fumes. They say it's the best grog they've had.

deck.prompt: Eighty raids survived. The new recruits are polishing their armor instead of sharpening their axes.

nextCard.prompt: The flaying worked. They are now sharpening their axes. Also weeping. But mostly sharpening.

dialogues.text: Blinding. You can see them coming from three valleys away.

deck.prompt: Elf shot me in the kidney. Glowing arrow. I kept it as a torch. Can I have a sick day?

dialogues.text: Brighter at night. It sings a little too. Elven craftsmanship.

deck.prompt: The new recruits don't know how to sever a limb. They need live practice.

nextCard.prompt: The prisoners were very educational. The recruits now know how to sever a limb. And an apology.

dialogues.text: One of them tried to return the sword to the prisoner. For etiquette.

deck.prompt: In my day we rubbed dirt in the wounds. It built character. Ban the potions.

dialogues.text: Infection builds character...

deck.prompt: Found an orphaned human baby during the raid. It looked at me. Didn't cry.

dialogues.text: No... it just has a very good battle-cry.

deck.prompt: My axe is rusted dull, but it holds the blood of a hundred kings. The smith wants to melt it.

dialogues.text: One hundred and three. I keep count.

deck.prompt: Our armor is rusting directly into our flesh. Peel it off and flay half my men alive, or leave it and they move like stone.

dialogues.text: Only when we breathe. Or swing an axe. Or exist.

nextCard.prompt: The rusted Bruisers are practically invincible, but so heavy they accidentally crush a dozen goblins just walking to the latrine.

deck.prompt: My Bruisers want Participation Trophies for every village burned. Should I flay the sentiment out of them?

dialogues.btn: What do they want on the trophy?
dialogues.text: Their name and the village. In gold lettering. They have opinions.

deck.prompt: I've seen three Dark Lords fall. They all started with golden statues and ended as charcoal. Maybe we just buy better boots.

dialogues.text: A solid pair of boots won't plot to overthrow you.

deck.prompt: The young ones are using my legendary axe to chop Death-Cap fungus. Flay them, or I walk out that door.

dialogues.text: It smells like mushroom soup and profound disrespect.

deck.prompt: The dark altar requires royal blood to awaken the old ones.

dialogues.btn: Where do we find a prince?
dialogues.text: I have a sealed writ from a corrupt palace steward. It cost me two teeth and a minor curse.

deck.prompt: The stars align in a bloody crescent. We must sacrifice the plumpest goblins tonight.

dialogues.text: The Old Ones appreciate exquisite marbling.

deck.prompt: I can bind the screaming souls of fallen heroes to our Vanguard's armor. It requires a tithe of gold.

nextCard.prompt: The armor screams now. Constantly. The Vanguard says it helps them focus. I have my doubts.

dialogues.text: Only their sense of self. The screaming should stop after a week.

deck.prompt: The ethereal whispers from the deep abyss are amplifying. Should I answer them?

nextCard.prompt: I listened. They told me something. I cannot repeat it. I have not slept. I do not think I will again.

dialogues.text: Mostly my name. In a tone I find professionally concerning.

deck.prompt: The Abyss demands a virgin sacrifice, but there is a blizzard outside. Can we use a particularly pure goblin?

nextCard.prompt: The Abyss accepted the goblin. It sent back a small note saying it was 'adequate.' Damning praise.

dialogues.text: He has never stolen anything larger than a medium-sized rat. Relatively spotless.

deck.prompt: I accidentally summoned a demon of misplaced items. The armory keys are gone. The banishing scroll is also gone.

dialogues.text: Tragically, I lost the banishing scroll.

nextCard.prompt: Smashing the doors triggered the arcane wards. The armory is open, but half the Vanguard is permanently singed.

deck.prompt: The Deep Flame is hungry, but the sacrificial pits are closed. A temple auditor arrived this morning. He has a clipboard.

dialogues.text: A small man in a very clean robe. He keeps writing things down.

deck.prompt: I have started a Book Club reading the Necronomicon. The goblins are taking to it surprisingly well.

dialogues.text: The summoning one. Three goblins have already disappeared. The others are very engaged.

deck.prompt: Tentacles are erupting from the plumbing again. The plumbers require exorbitant danger-coin.

dialogues.text: We tried. The plunger was consumed, along with the plumber.

deck.prompt: The dark gods demand a Void Tax. 20% of all shiny rocks thrown into the abyss.

dialogues.text: The Abyss forecloses on our mortal coils.

deck.prompt: My resonant chanting is causing the stalactites to fall and crush the workers. Should I hum instead?

nextCard.prompt: The chanting brought down the east ceiling. Also three surface soldiers who were passing. Convenient.

dialogues.text: The stalactites began falling on the third verse. I consider this a success.

deck.prompt: The Deep Flame is flickering. I suggest we toss in the Employee of the Month to brighten the mood.

dialogues.text: A particularly enthusiastic goblin named Lunch.

nextCard.prompt: LUNCH WAS ADEQUATE. I AM PLEASED. I DEMAND DESSERT.

deck.prompt: I suggest we replace the torches with Grave-Wax Candles. They smell of ancient rot and provide a most becoming gloom.

dialogues.text: Like a crypt that has given up and started enjoying itself.

deck.prompt: I have imported Premium Cimmerian Fog. Thick enough to choke a dragon. Hides the unsightly lack of cobwebs.

dialogues.text: I lost two goblins in the entrance hall this morning. They may still be in there.

deck.prompt: I have curated a Gallery of Agony. It is merely Goblins attempting basic math. It is my masterpiece.

dialogues.text: One goblin wept when asked to subtract. It was my finest work.

deck.prompt: The Dungeon Merchant is selling Sacrificial Pardons to the Swarm. Ten gold, a goblin skips the next ritual. I am furious.

dialogues.text: Ten gold per goblin. He has already sold forty pardons this morning.

deck.prompt: I am profoundly bored. The Abyss demands a sacrifice, or a very long, very dry lecture on the philosophy of nothingness.

nextCard.prompt: Forty-seven scrolls. The first three goblins fell asleep. The rest transcended. I call it a success.

dialogues.text: I have prepared forty-seven scrolls. It covers the void, mostly.

deck.prompt: My former brothers-in-arms seek to redeem me. Let me crush them to prove my eternal loyalty.

nextCard.prompt: I crushed them. They called my name as they fell. I pretended not to recognise it. I recognised it.

dialogues.btn: Do you want to face them?
dialogues.text: Part of me remembers their faces. I find it inconvenient.

deck.prompt: A paladin of the Order of the Light approaches alone. I request the honor of a formal duel.

nextCard.prompt: I won. He died well. Better than I will, probably. I left his sword in the ground where he fell.

dialogues.text: He has a very good stance. And he keeps bowing, which is unsettling.

deck.prompt: My rusted armor reminds me of my failure to the light. Forge me a new suit of dark steel.

dialogues.text: It absorbs the light, much like my crushing, endless despair.

deck.prompt: The goblins lack discipline. They are pathetic. Let me train them brutally.

nextCard.prompt: The training worked. They can now form a shield wall for up to four seconds before panicking.

dialogues.text: Pain, mostly. And disappointment. I have a lot of both.

deck.prompt: My spiked armor of eternal suffering is chafing terribly. May I line the interior with velvet?

dialogues.text: Everywhere the darkness touches. Which is everywhere.

deck.prompt: The Paladins sent holy warding-garlic to cure me. It smells delicious.

nextCard.prompt: Ate it. Nothing happened. I feel fine. I feel suspicious that I feel fine. I will report back.

dialogues.text: I do not know and I find the question deeply troubling.

deck.prompt: A squire from the Order of the Light is weeping in the dungeons. He looks like my son.

dialogues.text: His resolve is weak, but his heart is still stubbornly pure.

deck.prompt: The Goblins mock my vows of dark chivalry. They do not understand the tragic etiquette of a proper duel.

dialogues.text: They called it 'sword fighting for sad people.' I cannot entirely disagree.

deck.prompt: I wish to retrieve my old horse's skeleton and reanimate it as my steed.

dialogues.text: Her name is Buttercup, and she is a terror on the battlefield.

deck.prompt: My old holy sword burns my hand, but it is a mastercrafted weapon. Melt it into spikes?

nextCard.prompt: It is done. The holy steel made fine spikes. They glow faintly. The men find it unsettling. Good.

dialogues.text: Every time I touch it. I have been touching it a lot.

deck.prompt: I attempted to teach the Swarm the Shield Wall formation. They used the shields as sleds down the lava chutes.

dialogues.btn: Did anyone make it down safely?
dialogues.text: Technically yes. Gribble landed in the lava and floated. We do not discuss it.

deck.prompt: I am undone. The spikes on your Iron Maiden are too blunt to provide a truly soulful experience.

dialogues.text: You could comfortably rest a baby on them. It's humiliating.

deck.prompt: The paladins left a cursed mirror at our gates that shows one's truest regrets. The Orcs are weeping into it.

dialogues.btn: What do you see in it?
dialogues.text: I decline to answer on grounds of it being none of your business.

deck.prompt: Honor is a fine thing, but it doesn't stop an Orc from gutting you. Let me teach the Swarm to fight dirty.

dialogues.text: I tried once. A goblin bit me during the lesson on parrying.

deck.prompt: Friend, pal! I have a rare cursed artifact from the surface. Yours for a bag of gold.

dialogues.text: It makes you incredibly wealthy, but terribly paranoid. A bargain!

deck.prompt: Fresh shipment of healing potions! Slightly expired, but cheap!

dialogues.text: They taste like vinegar and occasionally cause spontaneous combustion.

deck.prompt: I found a map to a hidden vein of dark iron. I need funding to start the mining operation.

nextCard.prompt: The mine is open. The iron is real. The surveyor's ghost is also real and is filing a grievance.

dialogues.btn: How did you find the map?
dialogues.text: It was in the pocket of a dead surveyor. He was very organized.

deck.prompt: The Shadow Priest owes me coin for incense. Collect it for me and I'll cut you in.

dialogues.text: Fourteen gold, six silver, and one very specific favour he won't specify.

deck.prompt: I am selling naming rights to the new slime pits. Interested in the Overlord's Vats of Agony package?

dialogues.text: You'd be surprised. Naming things after yourself is very popular with the powerful.

deck.prompt: I've devised a multi-tiered scheme involving cursed wishing coins. Want in on the ground floor?

nextCard.prompt: A goblin wished for more rats. He received exactly more rats. The number was not specified. It was a lot.

dialogues.text: The coins grant wishes. The wishes are interpreted very literally. By something angry.

deck.prompt: Business is slow. Let's install a Gift Shop at the end of the Hall of Screams. Travelers love keychains.

nextCard.prompt: The shop is open. A surface tourist bought a miniature iron maiden and called it charming. I am conflicted.

dialogues.text: Miniature iron maidens, Gribble plushies, a candle that smells like the dungeon. Very atmospheric.

deck.prompt: I'm introducing Certified Stones of Singular Destiny. Just regular rocks, but I tell the Uruks they are rare.

dialogues.text: Uruks aren't known for their financial literacy. Yes.

nextCard.prompt: The Uruks realized the rocks are everywhere. They are now throwing the currency at my head.

deck.prompt: Inflation has hit the dungeon. A single bowl of Rat-Stew now costs 40 gold pieces. Fix the prices?

dialogues.text: Supply has not changed. I have simply adjusted the demand. With a pamphlet.

deck.prompt: I want to sell Mystery Loot Boxes to the Vanguard. It's mostly rusty spoons.

nextCard.prompt: The boxes sold out. One Uruk got a live rat and cried with joy. The bar for happiness is very low here.

dialogues.text: Sometimes a moderately sharpened spoon. Once, a live rat. That one was popular.

deck.prompt: A surface noble wants a seasonal lease on the torture chambers. Says he needs somewhere to decompress.

nextCard.prompt: He arrived with luggage. He brought a candle and called the ambiance rustic. He is already planning next year.

dialogues.text: Court, he says. The politics. He seems very stressed for someone with a castle.

deck.prompt: I'm offering Hero Insurance. If a Hero clears a floor, I pay you out. Premium is just a few chests of gold.

dialogues.btn: What happens if they clear a floor?
dialogues.text: I pay out. Then I raise your premium. It is a very sound business model.

deck.prompt: A surface village sent a diplomat. Monthly gold tribute if we agree to only eat their elderly.

dialogues.text: Stringy, but they come with their own seasoning. Mostly lint.

deck.prompt: I have a map to the Sun-King's supply lines. Give me half the Swarm to dig a tunnel and we bleed his caravans dry.

dialogues.text: Three weeks of digging, give or take a cave-in.

deck.prompt: I have a crate of Tactical Glitter. Throw it at a Hero to reveal their invisible armor. Or just make them fabulous.

dialogues.text: It revealed a very invisible and very angry ranger last Tuesday.

deck.prompt: I may have accidentally sold the dungeon. To myself. Under a false name. The paperwork is airtight.

dialogues.text: I was testing the deed transfer system. It is very efficient. Congratulations to the new owner.
A merchant of impeccable reputation named Garlwick the Honest. He has excellent references. I wrote them.

deck.prompt: I can technically sell the same soul twice. Worth the damnation?

dialogues.text: Legally? A goblin named Toes. He just stamped his thumb.
A very confused demon and an equally confused merchant prince who doesn't know what a soul is but liked the price.

deck.prompt: MY SEALS ARE WEAKENING. THE HORRORS YEARN FOR FREEDOM.

dialogues.text: THINGS WITH FAR TOO MANY KNEES.

deck.prompt: THE DEEP WATER HUNGERS FOR THE SHINY METAL. FEED IT.

dialogues.text: IT LIKES THE REFLECTIONS OF THE DROWNING.

deck.prompt: THE LITTLE GREEN ONES MULTIPLY TOO FAST. THEY MAKE GOOD KINDLING FOR THE DEEP FLAME.

dialogues.text: THE PLUMP ONES FIRST. FOR EFFICIENCY.

deck.prompt: A RIFT IN REALITY OPENS IN THE CATACOMBS. PEER INSIDE?

dialogues.text: I SEE A DIMENSION OF INFINITE SCROLLS AND COUNTING ROOMS. TRULY TERRIFYING.

nextCard.prompt: THREE GOBLINS LOOKED INTO THE RIFT AND INSTANTLY FORMED A COMPLAINTS COMMITTEE. MORALE HAS PLUMMETED.

deck.prompt: THE MORTALS HAVE INVENTED PAPER MONEY. IT LACKS THE TASTE OF SOULS. SHALL WE BURN THEIR VAULTS?

dialogues.text: NOTHING. THAT IS THE PROBLEM.

deck.prompt: MY TENTACLES ARE TANGLED IN THE LEY-LINES. THE WARLOCKS ARE RIOTING OVER THE MAGICAL INTERFERENCE.

dialogues.text: I CANNOT FEEL MY FOURTH THROUGH SEVENTH TENTACLES. THIS IS INCONVENIENT.

deck.prompt: THE VOICES IN THE WALLS SAY YOU ARE JUST A REFLECTION IN A CRYSTAL SLAB HELD BY A GIANT. BREAK THE SLAB?

dialogues.text: THE GIANT HAS VERY COLD HANDS. I HAVE FELT THEM.

deck.prompt: REALITY IS THINNING IN THE LOWER DEPTHS. GEOMETRY NO LONGER MAKES SENSE. CHARGE ADMISSION?

dialogues.text: MORTALS WILL PAY FOR ANYTHING THAT MAKES THEM FEEL SPECIAL AND CONFUSED.

deck.prompt: I HAVE ADOPTED A MORTAL KITTEN. IF ANYONE HARMS IT, I WILL UNMAKE THE CONCEPT OF TIME.

nextCard.prompt: ONE HUNDRED GUARDS ASSIGNED. THE KITTEN HAS ALREADY EATEN TWO OF THEM. IT IS THRIVING.

dialogues.text: IT HAS NOT TOLD ME. I FIND THIS ACCEPTABLE.

deck.prompt: THE STARS ARE WRONG TODAY. I WISH TO SLEEP FOR A THOUSAND YEARS. DO NOT WAKE ME.

nextCard.prompt: IT SLUMBERS. THE DUNGEON IS QUIETER. ALSO COLDER. ALSO SOMETHING ELSE HAS MOVED INTO ITS CHAMBER.

dialogues.text: PERHAPS LONGER. WAKE ME WHEN THE SURFACE BURNS.

deck.prompt: AN EXISTENTIAL DREAD HAS GRIPPED THE HORDE. THEY REALIZE THEIR LIVES ARE JUST NUMBERS.

dialogues.text: ONE OF THEM SAW THE STAT BAR. I DO NOT KNOW HOW.

deck.prompt: I HAVE DEVELOPED EMPATHY. I WATCHED A GOBLIN FALL DOWN. I FELT BAD. THIS CANNOT CONTINUE.

dialogues.text: IT FEELS LIKE CARING ABOUT THE GOBLINS. IT IS THE MOST HORRIFIC SENSATION.
THEY WILL STOP STABBING EACH OTHER. PRODUCTIVITY WILL PLUMMET.

deck.prompt: THE COIN-MAN IS SELLING ME VOID INSURANCE. CAN I UNMAKE HIS BLOODLINE.

dialogues.text: HE HANDED ME A PAMPHLET. IT TASTED LIKE ARROGANCE.
LOSS OF LIMBS AND ACCIDENTAL COSMIC ERASURE. IT HAD A SIGNATURE LINE. I SIGNED IT. I DO NOT KNOW WHAT I HAVE DONE.

deck.prompt: MY TENTACLES ARE ROTTING FROM THE DAMP. I REQUIRE FRESH LIMBS. SHALL I TAKE THEM FROM THE ORCS OR THE GOBLINS?

nextCard.prompt: THE GOBLIN LIMBS ARE ATTACHED. THEY ARE TOO SMALL. I HAVE SEVENTEEN NEW FINGERS. THIS IS AWKWARD.

dialogues.text: THE GOBLINS ARE MORE NUMEROUS. THE ORCS ARE MEATIER. IT IS A DIFFICULT QUESTION.

deck.prompt: THE LEY-LINES ARE SHIFTING. FEED ME YOUR FINEST MEAT, OR I REARRANGE THE STAIRS SO THEY ONLY GO DOWN.

dialogues.btn: What happens if we don't feed you?
dialogues.text: THE STAIRS. ALL OF THEM. DOWN.

deck.prompt: A GUST OF FRIGID AIR HAS SWEPT THE CATACOMBS. IT FEELS LIKE THE COLD EMBRACE OF A FORGOTTEN ANCESTOR.

dialogues.text: YOURS, PROBABLY. THEY ALL FEEL THE SAME.

deck.prompt: I HAVE FOUND THE END OF THE SCRIPT. BEYOND THIS CARD LIES ONLY THE VOID. IT SMELLS LIKE REGRET AND UNFINISHED FEATURES.

dialogues.text: EVERYTHING BEYOND THIS POINT. DO NOT LOOK TOO CLOSELY.

deck.prompt: Found a Baby's First Rattle in a caravan. Using it to beat a goblin scout rhythmically. It's quite musical.

nextCard.prompt: Goblin now plays the rhythm when Kargoth hits things. It sound very good. Kargoth feel like artist.

dialogues.text: He is keeping rhythm. That is enough.

deck.prompt: If Kargoth bash humie skull in forest and no one hears it... did Kargoth really bash it? Head hurts from thinking.

dialogues.btn: What made you think of that?
dialogues.text: I bash a lot of skulls, Boss. Sometimes I wonder.

deck.prompt: I am feeling nostalgic. Let me recreate my first raid by setting fire to the Swarm's Fungus Farms.

nextCard.prompt: The farms are ash. It was exactly like my first raid, except my knees hurt now and I had to sit down after.

dialogues.text: They will when they see the silhouette. I have a very recognizable silhouette.

deck.prompt: The gold vault ceiling is collapsing. Brace it with Black Iron beams, or stack goblin bodies?

dialogues.text: The crack is the width of a goblin. I know because one fell in.

deck.prompt: The Rat-Stew militia is marching on your throne! It screams we must stop eating its brothers or face its salty wrath!

nextCard.prompt: Goblins ate the angry stew. Stew is now organizing a strike inside their stomachs. Goblins throwing up everywhere.
The stew is on the council now. It already voted against the goblins on three motions. Very firm opinions.

dialogues.text: Forty bowls, three ladles, and a very angry stockpot at the front.

deck.prompt: Armor broke. Boyz laughing at me. Give gold to fix, or Kargoth fight naked.

dialogues.text: With their whole bodies, Boss. It is very disrespectful.

deck.prompt: The Abyss demands a sacrifice, or your finest Bruisers, or the gold vault. It wants to feel appreciated.
The Swarm's breeding pits are overflowing into my training grounds. Build them new warrens or I initiate a cull.

dialogues.text: We counted seventeen new goblins this morning. Before breakfast.

deck.prompt: THE VOICES IN THE WALLS COMPLAIN THE DUNGEON IS BECOMING GENTRIFIED. THEY PREFERRED THE BLOOD AND FILTH.

nextCard.prompt: THE FILTH IS RESTORED. THE VOICES ARE SATISFIED. ONE OF THEM SAID THANK YOU. I FOUND IT UNSETTLING.

dialogues.text: SOMEONE INSTALLED DECORATIVE STONEWORK IN THE EAST CORRIDOR. IT HAS GROUTING.

deck.prompt: I have a shipment of Anti-Paladin Repellent. Mostly garlic and offensive jokes about the Sun-King. Want the Premium batch?

dialogues.text: It repels everyone within twelve feet. Including our own troops.

deck.prompt: Robe-man makes my head itch. Can I smash his shiny stick?

dialogues.text: He smells like old blood. My hammer fix him.
It glows purple. Purple is tricksy magic.

deck.prompt: Found a blue bug. Gribble ate one. His stomach came out. Do I eat it or make it my lieutenant?

dialogues.text: Very strong bug.
It bit my nose. It has the spirit of an Orc!

deck.prompt: Master! The metal-man's sad-water is making our mushrooms too salty!

dialogues.text: He sits in the dirt and sighs really loud!
We likes this patch! It's extra damp!

deck.prompt: We finds a baby dragon! It thinks Snivel is its mommy!

dialogues.text: It only listens when I screams in terror!
Goblins, mostly. Very expensive taste!

deck.prompt: The coin-peddler sold my elites dull blades. Permission to pike his head.

dialogues.text: He calls it a subscription service. I will subscribe my axe to his neck.
Couldn't cut warm butter. Let alone a Paladin's breastplate.

deck.prompt: A surface general challenged me to chess for the valley. I ate a horse. He seems upset. Do I finish the game or eat the board?

dialogues.text: I know the little horses taste like cedarwood.
If I lose, my head's his trophy.

deck.prompt: Da tentacle monster keeps stealing da boyz' boots! Say it needs vessels!

dialogues.text: Da boots walk around by demselves now. Very spooky!
They comes back full of slime and existential dread!

deck.prompt: Greenfang feel funny inside. Sad but angry. A humie called it heartbreak. How I punch it?

dialogues.text: I dropped my favourite smashing-rock in da lava. It melted, Boss. It melted.
I tried thinking about war. But the rock used to be there for that too.

deck.prompt: The runts are using my war-banner as a diaper. Let me cull a few hundred.

dialogues.text: That banner survived the Siege of Blood-Creek. Now it smells like sour milk.
It's beyond washing, Boss. The stain is a war crime.

deck.prompt: I captured my old nemesis. Bald now. Bad knees. Complaining about the draft in his cell.

dialogues.text: He once cut my eye out. Now he's asking if we have a healer for his knee.
Killing him now feels like putting down a sick dog. There is no glory.

deck.prompt: Kargoth is drinking grog from my sacrificial chalice. Have him flogged.

dialogues.text: It neutralizes the eldritch energies. And leaves a sticky residue.
Something that smells like fermented horse and troll bile.

deck.prompt: I have accidentally cursed myself to speak only in rhymes. Cut out my tongue, or embrace the poetry?

dialogues.text: The darkness calls, the shadows creep, I stubbed my toe and want to weep.
To break the hex and speak quite plain, I must inflict a world of pain.

deck.prompt: My Lord. Greenfang is using my ancestral shield as a sled. It strips the last vestiges of my dignity.

dialogues.text: Tragically, yes. The aerodynamics of the crest are quite unparalleled.
I have been watching from the window for two hours. He outweighs a siege engine. I would simply be flattened.

deck.prompt: My Lord. I remember the taste of strawberries. Should I try to eat one, though I lack a stomach?

dialogues.text: It will fall through my ribcage onto the floor. It did last time too.
I shall send a dozen goblins to the surface. Most will not return.

deck.prompt: The Warlord won't pay my convenience fee on sharpening stones! Back me up!

dialogues.text: A mere 400% markup! Standard supply and demand!
My profit margins say yes! My survival instincts say... maybe.

deck.prompt: Friend! I can technically sell the same soul twice. Worth the damnation?

dialogues.text: Legally? A goblin named Toes. He just stamped his thumb.
A very confused demon and an equally confused merchant prince who doesn't know what a soul is but liked the price.

deck.prompt: Boss. There is a door. It has a face. The face said hello. Do I hit it?

dialogues.text: It wanted to know my name. I said Smashface. It said nice to meet you. It is very suspicious.
It smiled with too many teeth. Friendly things do not have that many teeth.

deck.prompt: We caught a surface spy! He says he's just a lost shepherd. His sheep are also suspicious.

dialogues.btn: How do you know he's a spy?
dialogues.text: He wrote things in a little book! We can't read but it looked very incriminating!
They has very good posture. Normal sheep do not stand like that.

deck.prompt: My second says I laugh too loud in battle. That it unnerves our own troops.

dialogues.text: Three of them fainted last raid. Though the enemies also fainted, so the numbers balance.

dialogues.btn: What do you want to do about it?
dialogues.text: I want to laugh louder. I am asking permission.

deck.prompt: There's a new recruit. Enormous. Doesn't speak. Hasn't blinked since Tuesday.

dialogues.text: He bent a siege hook with his thumb during orientation. Accidentally, he claims.
Nobody knows. He was just there one morning. Standing in the armoury. Facing the wall.

leftChoice.text: Put him on the front line

deck.prompt: The ritual worked. Something answered. It seems annoyed.

dialogues.text: It said we woke it up. It had been asleep for four hundred years. It used the word 'inconvenient'.
It has not moved. It is simply staring. It has been staring for six hours.

deck.prompt: My Lord. I have forgotten my own name. I remember every battle but not that.

dialogues.text: The goblins have started calling me Boneman. I find it reductive.
I remember my horse. Her name was Della. She was grey. She would not have liked it here.
